nodes.name: Immanuel Kant
nodes.d: Immanuel Kant was a German philosopher. Born in Königsberg in the Kingdom of Prussia, he is considered one of the central thinkers of the Enlightenment.

nodes.name: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel
nodes.d: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel was a German philosopher and a major figure in the tradition of German idealism.

nodes.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
nodes.d: Friedrich Wilhelm Nietzsche was a German philosopher and writer who started his career as a classical philologist and turned to philosophy early in his academic career.

nodes.name: Karl Marx
nodes.d: Karl Marx was a German philosopher, social and political theorist, and revolutionary socialist.

nodes.name: Martin Buber
nodes.d: Martin Buber was an Austrian-Israeli philosopher best known for his philosophy of dialogue, a form of existentialism centered on the distinction between the I–Thou relationship and the I–It relationship.

nodes.name: Vladimir Solovyov (philosopher)
nodes.d: Vladimir Sergeyevich Solovyov was a Russian philosopher, theologian, poet, pamphleteer, and literary critic, who played a significant role in the development of Russian philosophy and poetry at the end of the 19th century and in the spiritual renaissance of the early 20th century.

nodes.name: Mikhail Bakhtin
nodes.d: Mikhail Mikhailovich Bakhtin was a Russian philosopher and literary critic who worked on the philosophy of language, ethics, and literary theory.

nodes.name: Ivan Ilyin
nodes.d: Ivan Alexandrovich Ilyin was a Russian jurist, religious and political philosopher, publicist, orator, and a far-right thinker.

nodes.name: Franz Rosenzweig
nodes.d: Franz Rosenzweig was a German theologian, philosopher, and translator.

nodes.name: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz
nodes.d: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz was a German polymath active as a mathematician, philosopher, scientist, and diplomat who is credited, alongside Isaac Newton, with the creation of calculus in addition to many other branches of mathematics, such as binary arithmetic and statistics.

nodes.name: Baruch Spinoza
nodes.d: Baruch Spinoza, also known under his Latinized pen name Benedictus de Spinoza, was a philosopher of Portuguese-Jewish origin who was born and lived in the Dutch Republic.

nodes.name: René Descartes
nodes.d: René Descartes was a French philosopher, mathematician, and scientist whose work was foundational to mathematics and modern philosophy.

nodes.name: Voltaire
nodes.d: François-Marie Arouet, known by his pen name Voltaire, was a French Enlightenment writer, philosopher, satirist, and historian.

nodes.name: Ralph Cudworth
nodes.d: Ralph Cudworth was an English Anglican clergyman, Christian Hebraist, classicist, theologian and philosopher, and a leading figure among the Cambridge Platonists who became 11th Regius Professor of Hebrew, 26th Master of Clare Hall, and 14th Master of Christ's College.

nodes.name: Henry More
nodes.d: Henry More was an English philosopher, Anglican priest, theologian, and poet, associated with the Cambridge Platonists.

nodes.name: Henry Brougham, 1st Baron Brougham and Vaux
Edward Herbert, 1st Baron Herbert of Cherbury
Aristotle
nodes.d: Aristotle was an ancient Greek philosopher and polymath.

nodes.name: Thomas Aquinas
nodes.d: Thomas Aquinas was an Italian Dominican friar and priest, theologian, and philosopher.

nodes.name: Augustine of Hippo
nodes.d: Augustine of Hippo, also well-known as Saint Augustine, was a Christian theologian and philosopher from Thagaste, Numidia Cirtensis and the Bishop of Hippo Regius.

nodes.name: John Scotus Eriugena
nodes.d: John Scotus Eriugena, also known as Johannes Scotus Erigena, John the Scot or John the Irish-born, was an Irish Neoplatonist philosopher, theologian and poet of the Early Middle Ages.

nodes.name: Alcuin
nodes.d: Alcuin of York, also called Ealhwine, Alhwin, or Alchoin, was an Anglo-Saxon scholar, clergyman, poet, and teacher from York, Northumbria, who was active in the Carolingian Empire in the 8th century.

nodes.name: Bertrand Russell
nodes.d: Bertrand Arthur William Russell, 3rd Earl Russell, was an English philosopher, logician, and social reformer.

nodes.name: William James
nodes.d: William James was an American philosopher and psychologist.

nodes.name: John Stuart Mill
nodes.d: John Stuart Mill was an English philosopher, political economist, and politician.

nodes.name: B. R. Ambedkar
nodes.d: Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar was an Indian jurist, economist, social reformer and politician who chaired the committee that drafted the Constitution of India based on the debates of the Constituent Assembly of India and the first draft of Sir Benegal Narsing Rau.

nodes.name: Ferdinand de Saussure
nodes.d: Ferdinand Mongin de Saussure was a Swiss linguist, semiotician and philosopher.

nodes.name: Plato
nodes.d: Plato was an ancient Greek philosopher of Classical Athens who is most commonly considered the foundational thinker of the Western philosophical tradition.

nodes.name: Diogenes Laertius
nodes.d: Diogenes Laërtius was a biographer of the Greek philosophers.

nodes.name: Heraclitus
nodes.d: Heraclitus was a pre-Socratic Greek philosopher from the city of Ephesus, which was then part of the Persian Empire.

nodes.name: Luc de Clapiers, marquis de Vauvenargues
Madhvacharya
nodes.d: Madhvacharya, also known as Purna Prajna and Ānanda Tīrtha, was an Indian philosopher, theologian and the chief proponent of the Dvaita school of Vedanta.

nodes.name: The Buddha
nodes.d: Siddhartha Gautama, most commonly referred to as the Buddha, was a wandering religious teacher who lived in the eastern Indo-Gangetic Plains during the 6th or 5th century BCE and founded Buddhism.

nodes.name: Adi Shankara
nodes.d: Adi Shankara, also called Adi Shankaracharya, was an Indian Vedic scholar-monk, philosopher, and teacher of Advaita Vedanta.

nodes.name: Je Tsongkhapa
nodes.d: Tsongkhapa was an influential Tibetan Buddhist monk, philosopher, and tantric yogi, whose activities led to the formation of the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism.

nodes.name: Uddālaka Āruṇi
nodes.d: Uddalaka Aruni, also referred to as Uddalaka or Aruni or Uddalaka Varuni, was a revered Vedic sage of Hinduism.

nodes.name: Yajnavalkya
nodes.d: Yajnavalkya or Yagyavalkya is a Hindu Vedic sage prominently mentioned in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad and Tattiriya Upanishad.

nodes.name: Guifeng Zongmi
nodes.d: Guifeng Zongmi was a Tang dynasty Chinese Buddhist monk and scholar who is considered a patriarch of both the Huayan school and Chan Buddhism.

nodes.name: Max Müller
nodes.d: Friedrich Max Müller was a German-born British comparative philologist and Orientalist.

nodes.name: Gaudapada
nodes.d: Gauḍapāda, also referred as Gauḍapādācārya, was an early medieval era Hindu philosopher and scholar of the Advaita Vedanta school of Hindu philosophy.

nodes.name: Sanjaya Belatthiputta
nodes.d: Sañjaya Belatthiputra, was an Indian ascetic philosopher who lived around the 7th-6th century BC in the region of Magadha.

nodes.name: Maitreyi
nodes.d: Maitreyi was an Indian philosopher who lived during the later Vedic period in ancient India.

nodes.name: Avicenna
nodes.d: Ibn Sina, commonly known in the West as Avicenna ( AV-ih-SEN-ə), was a preeminent philosopher and physician of the Muslim world.

nodes.name: Maimonides
nodes.d: Moses ben Maimon, commonly known as Maimonides and also referred to by the Hebrew acronym Rambam, was a Sephardic Jewish rabbi who is widely acknowledged as one of the most prolific and influential Torah scholars of the Middle Ages.

nodes.name: Al-Farabi
nodes.d: Abu Nasr Muhammad al-Farabi, known in the Latin West as Alpharabius, was an early Islamic philosopher and music theorist.

nodes.name: Ibn Taymiyya
nodes.d: Ibn Taymiyya was a Sunni Muslim scholar, jurist, Mujtahid, traditionist, Qadiri Sufi, proto-Salafist theologian and iconoclast.

nodes.name: Ibn Hazm
nodes.d: Ibn Ḥazm was an Andalusi Muslim polymath, historian, traditionist, jurist, philosopher, and theologian, born in the Córdoban Caliphate, present-day Spain.

nodes.name: Ibn Arabi
nodes.d: Ibn 'Arabī was a Sunni Muslim Arab scholar, Sufi mystic, poet, and Muslim philosopher from al-Andalus, who exercised notable influence within Sufi metaphysics and Islamic thought in general.

nodes.name: Abu Hatim Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Razi
Confucius
nodes.d: Confucius, born Kong Qiu, was a Chinese philosopher of the Spring and Autumn period who is traditionally considered the paragon of Chinese sages.

nodes.name: Mencius
nodes.d: Mencius, born Meng Ke, was a Chinese Confucian philosopher, often described as the Second Sage to reflect his traditional esteem relative to Confucius himself.

nodes.name: Zhu Xi
nodes.d: Zhu Xi, formerly romanized Chu Hsi, was a Chinese philosopher, historian, politician, poet, and calligrapher of the Southern Song dynasty.

nodes.name: Laozi
nodes.d: Laozi is the name traditionally given to an ancient Chinese philosopher, also identified as Li Er or Lao Dan, who is regarded as the author or originating teacher associated with the Tao Te Ching, one of the foundational texts of Taoism.
